BiblicalUsage: Peter and James both say the flower of the grass falls and withers, and the glory of man is as the flower of the field. The word is the blossom itself, brief and bright and gone.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for a flower holds no doctrine of its own; its lesson is the apostles', that the glory of man fades like grass, and only the word of the Lord endures.
RelatedPeople: Simon Peter; James, Brother of Jesus
